title: Feature-Adaptive Fusion in Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Networks for Robust Biomedical Image Classification
authors: Yan-Yan Hou, Jian Li, Chongqiang Ye, Hengji Li, Zhuo Wang, Qinghui Liu
abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical neural networks provide a promising approach for incorporating quantum circuits into machine learning in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum regime. However, existing hybrid models often rely on fixed or globally shared fusion strategies, which may limit their ability to exploit complementary information carried by quantum branches, especially under distribution shifts. In this work, we propose a Feature-Adaptive Fusion Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network (FAF-HQNN) for biomedical image classification. The model combines a classical deep feature encoder with a variational quantum circuit (VQC) and introduces a feature-adaptive fusion mechanism to dynamically weight classical and quantum predictions. We evaluate FAF-HQNN on two MedMNIST benchmarks, PathMNIST and BloodMNIST, under clean and corrupted test conditions. FAF-HQNN achieves the strongest overall performance on clean data among the compared methods and shows improved robustness under Gaussian, salt-and-pepper, and Poisson corruptions. Further analysis of circuit layout, measurement basis, and depth shows that even shallow variational quantum circuits can provide useful complementary information. These results demonstrate that feature-adaptive fusion is an effective strategy for improving accuracy and robustness in hybrid quantum-classical models for biomedical image classification.
summary: This paper proposes the Feature-Adaptive Fusion Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network (FAF-HQNN) for biomedical image classification. It addresses the weakness of fixed fusion methods by dynamically weighting classical and quantum predictions based on input features. The model shows superior accuracy and robustness compared to existing methods, validating adaptive fusion in hybrid quantum-classical AI.
main_problem: The paper aims to improve the robustness of biomedical image classification by effectively integrating the complementary strengths of quantum and classical computation.
main_result: The proposed Feature-Adaptive Fusion Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network (FAF-HQNN) achieves state-of-the-art performance on clean data and demonstrates significantly improved robustness against various classical corruptions.
method: It introduces a feature-adaptive fusion mechanism that dynamically weights the predictions from a classical deep encoder and a variational quantum circuit (VQC).
model_or_system: The model is a Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network (HQNN) combining a ResNet-18 classical encoder with a VQC. The core innovation is the adaptive fusion layer that learns to optimally combine the classical and quantum outputs based on input features.
key_observables: Predictive accuracy, robustness under Gaussian, salt-and-pepper, and Poisson corruptions, and performance metrics (ACC, Precision, Recall, F1-score, AUC).
important_parameters: Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) regime, feature-adaptive fusion coefficients, and classical corruption types.
main_assumptions: The performance gains are demonstrated on controlled MedMNIST benchmarks, and quantum noise analysis is based on simulation rather than real hardware.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the overall FAF-HQNN pipeline, including feature extraction and the adaptive fusion structure. Figure 2 details the quantum branch architecture, from data encoding to readout.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the limitation of fixed fusion strategies in HQNNs. It then proposes the FAF-HQNN architecture, detailing the feature compression and adaptive fusion mechanism. Finally, it evaluates the model on clean and corrupted MedMNIST benchmarks, followed by supplementary analysis on quantum noise sensitivity.
why_interesting: The work directly applies quantum circuits (VQC) to a machine learning task, providing concrete evidence of how quantum feature extraction can enhance classical AI models, which is a key area of quantum information research.

figures.caption: Fig. 1: Overall framework of the proposed FAF-HQNN model. (a) Pipeline of FAF- HQNN. Input biomedical images are first preprocessed and then fed into the feature extraction module, followed by a feature compression module for quantum-compatible embedding. The resulting shared embedding is subsequently passed to feature-adaptive fusion module, including a quantum branch, a feature-adaptive class-wise fusion mech- anism, and a classical branch, whose outputs are combined to produce the final prediction.
